Yes, decisional algorithms can replace global introspection in the individual causality assessment of spontaneously reported Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs). 

Decisional algorithms, such as the Naranjo algorithm or the Bayesian algorithm, provide a systematic and standardized approach to assessing the causality of ADRs. They use a set of predefined criteria and questions to evaluate the relationship between the drug and the adverse event, reducing the subjectivity associated with global introspection. 

These algorithms can help improve the consistency, reliability, and transparency of causality assessments, making them a useful tool in pharmacovigilance and drug safety evaluation.
